spans.claim: Ponsonby Paget was found dead with a stab wound in his study
spans.anchor: Ponsonby Paget lay on the floor near his writing-table
spans.span: Ponsonby Paget lay on the floor near his writing-table.

spans.claim: A walking-stick was found beneath an overturned table at the crime scene
spans.anchor: Green, who had been poking delicately about among the wreckage of furniture, pulled out a walking-stick from beneath an overturned table
spans.span: Green, who had been poking delicately about among the wreckage of furniture, pulled out a walking-stick from beneath an overturned table.

spans.claim: The walking-stick belonged to Alexander David Kinloch
spans.anchor: It was Kinloch's stick. It was the stick the policeman had handed back to him
spans.span: It was Kinloch's stick. It was the stick the policeman had handed back to him on my doorstep a few hours earlier.

spans.claim: Kinloch was blind and used the walking-stick to feel his way
spans.anchor: A blind man and his stick are inseparable
spans.span: A blind man and his stick are inseparable, and I had seen him with it lying across his knees all the time he had been in my study.

spans.claim: Sir Stephen Wye had a strong motive to kill Ponsonby Paget
spans.anchor: Wye, of course, went to see Paget about it, and there learned that Paget had acquired certain information about him which if published would wreck his political ambitions
spans.span: Wye, of course, went to see Paget about it, and there learned that Paget had acquired certain information about him which if published would wreck his political ambitions.

spans.claim: The murderer left no footprints but car tracks with embedded cartridge

spans.claim: Kinloch was forcibly removed from the murder scene
spans.anchor: He was carried off by some one--oh, yes--by some one who may very well have been unaware he was blind
spans.span: He was carried off by some one--oh, yes--by some one who may very well have been unaware he was blind, and who supposed the blind man would be certain to know him at sight.

spans.claim: Lady Wye fainted near Kinloch and was emotionally involved
spans.anchor: The breakdown was at once so utter and so unexpected that it amazed Kinloch

spans.anchor: The operation for corneitis was performed by Sir Donald Fyffe in Edinburgh, and one week later Kinloch got his first glimpse of the light again

spans.claim: Dick Hollins was a red herring suspect

spans.claim: Kinloch was found sitting in Enderby Gardens reading Braille
spans.anchor: He was sitting against the railings on a short three-legged camp-stool, the usual large volume on his knees

spans.claim: The murderer is Sir Stephen Wye
spans.anchor: Wye was our man right enough

spans.claim: The murder was committed by an expert with a knife
spans.anchor: The hand that sent that knife to the heart was expert--accustomed to the use of it
spans.span: I'll tell you this, Green, the hand that sent that knife to the heart was expert--accustomed to the use of it.

spans.claim: The room was lit during the murder
spans.anchor: You are forgetting the mirror. He would hardly take out a mirror in darkness

spans.claim: The false assumption that the murderer was lame is refuted

spans.claim: The trap to catch the murderer involves Kinloch waiting in public
spans.anchor: He will wait in some road or street he has heard her mention more than once, wait for her to come along

spans.claim: The murderer tried to escape by car but crashed over a cliff
spans.anchor: The car struck a projecting spur of the cliff and, passing on with one head-light out, left behind it a cloud of white dust
